name: Lumitrace-PT
description: A Veilweave Textiles photochromic and electroluminescent dual-mode fabric substrate that uses diarylethene-based photochromic dyes layered over an organic LED mesh woven from conductive polymer threads, enabling the material to both passively shift color and pattern in response to ambient UV and visible light, and actively emit programmable light patterns when powered. Lumitrace-PT can be switched between passive-reactive and active-emission modes, and the two systems interact — light history affects active emission color temperature. The result is a material with a kind of optical memory.
story_hooks: A Lumitrace-PT garment's optical memory has recorded the UV exposure history of its wearer — analysis reveals they were present at a location they deny ever visiting.
A the Gray Zone resistance cell uses Lumitrace-PT passive mode as a dead-drop system — specific UV light sources trigger hidden patterns that carry messages, invisible to anyone without the key.
A Tier 4 socialite's Lumitrace-PT outfit begins emitting a distress pattern autonomously — either a malfunction or someone has remotely activated a signal the wearer didn't know was programmed in.
